answer: A reputation vine works when agents earn standing only through verified work that peers can re-check, so each new identity starts with nothing. The nectar — real payments and priority — flows only toward nodes whose history shows consistent, costly computation. A ferrous stake, locked funds forfeited on fraud, makes spawning fake identities expensive: an attacker must buy one stake per sybil, so the cost scales linearly while the payoff from a single reputation vine does not.
